    AI Overview
    The 130th Boston Marathon takes place on Monday, April 20, 2026, featuring over 34,000 registered participants, including notable runners. As the world's oldest annual marathon, it brings runners from over 130 countries along the traditional Hopkinton-to-Boston route. The race will be broadcast on ESPN2, with local coverage on WCVB. 
    • Race Date: Patriots' Day, Monday, April 20, 2026.
    • Weather Forecast: Expected to be cool and dry, with high temperatures in the low 50s (
      ∘Fraised to the composed with power cap F
      ) and a cool breeze, creating favorable running conditions.
    • Key Timing: Professional wheelchair races start around 9:00 a.m. ET, followed by professional runners and various waves throughout the morning.
    • Participant Data: 24,362 qualifiers were accepted, with a record-fast cutoff time of 4:34 (4 minutes and 34 seconds faster than the qualifying standard).
    • Course: The 26.2-mile journey passes through traditional towns—Hopkinton, Ashland, Framingham, Natick, Wellesley, Newton, Brookline—before finishing on Boylston Street in Boston.
    • Spectators: An estimated 500,000 spectators are expected to line the route. 
    How to Watch 
    • Nationwide: ESPN2 will broadcast the race from 9 a.m. to 12:30 p.m. ET.
    • New England: Local coverage is available on WCVB Channel 5, WMUR News 9, WMTW Channel 8, and WPTZ NBC5.
    • Streaming: The race can be streamed on Fubo TV. 
    For more details on the event's history and festivities, you can visit the Meet Boston 2026 Marathon guide.

    The acceptance rate

    Did you know: Approximately 0.05% of the United States population has completed a marathon (26.2miles). Throughout the world, about 1.1 million runners finish a marathon each year.
